body.statement: For every fixed member of \(\mathfrak M\), can the handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{fin}}\) establish, uniformly over \(\beta\in\mathcal K\), exact ties, arbitrary balanced deterministic baseline lattices, local action displacements of order \(m^{-1/2}\), and unequal inclusion probabilities, that the finite Horvitz--Thompson action regret on \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) differs from the continuous-coarea Gaussian boundary quadratic form of \(G_{\infty}\) by \(o(m^{-1})\) in probability over the split, and that the contrast between \(T_n^{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}\) has no additional lattice or inclusion correction at order \(m/n^2+1/(nm)\)?
body.justification: This is the proof boundary on which the advertised second-order constant is valid or must acquire a finite-randomization correction.
body.gap: Li and Ding provide a first-order random-partition central limit theorem, and Wang and Li provide quantitative Gaussian control for best-choice rerandomization; neither controls score-weighted moving-boundary moments at this scale.
body.consumer: A positive answer validates smooth pilot rules on integer-valued manufacturing baselines; a negative answer identifies the correction planners must include.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether, for every fixed model member, score-weighted moving-boundary moments and exact unequal-inclusion covariance admit the required \(\beta\)-uniform little-oh comparison on arbitrary bounded deterministic baseline lattices.
obligation.obstruction: The proved atom-safe lower-tail identity is exact at a fixed law but gives no quantitative comparison between a shrinking finite assignment boundary and its Gaussian limit. Ordinary Berry--Esseen control of unweighted probabilities is not the weighted second-order estimate requested here.
obligation.attempted: Used the exact lower-tail primal-dual identity to neutralize fixed-law ties and decomposed the Horvitz--Thompson correction around uniform marginals. The latter would be order two under a uniform leave-one-unit inclusion bound of order one over the wave size, but that bound is not derivable from the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result: The proved lower-tail identity shows that randomized ties and atoms do not themselves create a sign correction: at any fixed finite law the exact lower-tail rule minimizes the trimmed linear score.  For a local displacement of size \(m^{-1/2}\), it remains necessary to compare score-weighted symmetric differences of two moving quadratic sublevel sets and the exact unequal-inclusion Horvitz--Thompson covariance with their Gaussian counterparts at error \(o(m^{-1})\).  The frozen boundedness and weak empirical convergence assumptions supply no stated quantitative theorem of this strength.
